title: AI Solutions Architect
summary: Designs enterprise AI systems end to end: model selection, retrieval architecture, agents, security, cost and the integration into existing line-of-business platforms. The natural destination for an enterprise .NET architect who adds applied AI depth.
twoHundredKPotential: Realistic within 12–24 months of the transition at a mid-to-large enterprise or consultancy, especially with a delivered portfolio and an Azure AI certification.
salarySource: Aggregated public US ranges (Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Indeed, Dice). Estimates only — update via Admin.
demandNotes: Every large enterprise is now standing up AI platforms and almost none have architects who understand both the model layer and existing enterprise integration. That overlap is the scarce commodity.
aiRiskNotes: The role exists because of AI and is defined by judgement: trade-offs, cost, risk and stakeholder alignment. Models accelerate the work rather than replace the decision-maker.
responsibilities: Translate business problems into AI solution architectures with explicit assumptions and success measures
Select models, retrieval strategies and vector stores, and defend the choice against alternatives
Design the AI gateway layer: routing, rate limits, caching, failover across providers, token budgets
Own the security design: identity, secrets, PII handling, prompt-injection defence, audit and data residency
Produce cost models and keep production spend inside them
Set standards for evaluation, groundedness measurement and regression testing of AI features
Lead technical design reviews and mentor engineering teams through delivery
Present architecture and trade-offs to executive and technical audiences
interviewFocus: Design an enterprise RAG system over 500,000 documents with per-user permissions
Explain chunking strategy, embedding choice and why reranking changes answer quality
How would you prevent prompt injection in a system that reads untrusted email?
Model a monthly cost for 50,000 AI requests and explain what you would cut first
Multi-provider failover: what breaks, and how do you keep behaviour consistent?
How do you measure whether an AI feature got better or worse between releases?

title: Cloud Security Architect
summary: Owns the security architecture of cloud platforms: identity, network segmentation, secrets, data protection, zero trust and compliance. Pays at the top of the market and is structurally hard to automate.
twoHundredKPotential: Strong. Security architecture commands a premium, and regulated industries pay above these ranges for people who can also write code.
salarySource: Aggregated public US ranges (Levels.fyi, Glassdoor, Indeed, Dice). Estimates only — update via Admin.
demandNotes: Cloud estates keep growing, regulation keeps tightening, and AI workloads have opened an entirely new attack surface that few security architects understand yet.
aiRiskNotes: Accountability cannot be delegated to a model. AI assists with detection and review; the architecture decisions and the regulatory sign-off remain human.
responsibilities: Design zero-trust identity and network architecture across cloud estates
Threat model applications and platforms, including AI workloads
Define secrets management, encryption and key rotation standards
Own compliance mapping and evidence for audits
Review and approve architecture from a security standpoint
Lead incident response design and detection engineering standards
interviewFocus: Design zero-trust access for a multi-tenant SaaS platform on Azure
How do you secure an LLM application that ingests untrusted documents?
Explain your approach to secrets across 200 microservices
Walk through a threat model for a payment processing pipeline
